name: example-codon-plugin
summary: Exaloop's own worked example of a Codon plugin, called MyValidate. A single validate.cpp registers an IR pass that inserts a call to validate() after every call to foo(), with a plugin.toml and a CMake build alongside it. First-party rather than a user, and the reference every third-party plugin in this index is written against.
why_codon: README states the repo implements an example plugin for Codon, including a Codon IR pass.
note: First-party. Arguably belongs with the anchors rather than in the entry set; recorded here with a first_party flag pending his call.

name: GeneticEngine
summary: A framework for genetic programming over user-defined grammars. Codon is an opt-in accelerator for the example suite rather than a dependency: setting CODON=1 makes run_examples.sh attempt codon run -release per example, guarded by a can_run_with_codon check that skips anything pulling in heavy third-party modules, and falls back to running under Python otherwise. The most careful treatment of Codon's library limits found in the index -- it encodes them as a runtime decision instead of assuming them.
why_codon: run_examples.sh comments state Codon is attempted when requested and fallen back on for packages Codon does not support, with a heuristic that Codon generally does not handle heavy third-party modules.
note: Codon source is .py; found through the invocation lane, not extension:codon.

name: Language_Reactor
summary: A cross-language benchmark harness with a web front end, running the same prime-computation workload through many toolchains. Codon is one of them, built ahead of time with codon build -release -exe over the shared prime.py, so it is measured against interpreted Python rather than standing in for it.
why_codon: The runner defines a python_codon target that prints codon --version and compiles the shared benchmark with codon build -release -exe.
note: Codon source is .py; found through the invocation lane.

name: word-counter
summary: A three-way benchmark of the same word-counting workload in Python, Codon and Go, with a Nix flake pinning the toolchains. The runner times each and extracts the reported execution time, so the comparison is reproducible rather than anecdotal.
why_codon: README states the repo benchmarks python, codon and go; the runner invokes codon run -release on benchmark/codon/wordcount.py.
note: Codon source is .py. Also carries a Nix flake referencing the Codon release, so it appears in both round-2 signals.

name: atcoder-codon
summary: A ready-made competitive-programming environment for AtCoder built on Python 3.13 and Codon, shipped as a published container image with a devcontainer definition and a workflow that builds and publishes it. Documented in English and Japanese. Packaging Codon for a specific audience rather than using it for a problem.
why_codon: README states the environment is for solving AtCoder problems using Python 3.13 and Codon, described there as a high-performance Python compiler.
note: Third competitive-programming entry after takechi-scratch/atcoder and Jutge.org, and the only one that packages an environment for others.

name: E++
summary: A project to build a Python-compatible compiled language, readable like Python and native in performance. Codon is the backend rather than a comparison: a Rust src/codon module holds an installer, a configuration layer, a backend and a runner, so the tool manages a Codon toolchain on the user's behalf and compiles through it.
why_codon: README states the goal of a fully Python-compatible language with native performance; the Rust codon module supplies the installer, backend and runner that deliver it.
note: Second project after codonx to wrap Codon in a tool written in another language, and the more ambitious of the two: it presents Codon as its own language.

name: University (compilers activity)
summary: A university coursework archive. Its programming-languages module carries an activity comparing compilers against interpreters, and Codon appears there as one implementation of the binary-trees benchmark, driven from a Makefile alongside the other languages.
why_codon: The activity is titled as a comparison of compilers and interpreters, and the Makefile runs the Codon build beside the others.

name: RioKKH/MachineLearning
summary: A personal machine-learning working repository with a Codon directory holding a Fibonacci example and a matplotlib script. The runner exports CODON_PYTHON to a static libpython before invoking codon run -release, which is what plotting from Codon requires.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from a Codon directory holding a Fibonacci benchmark and a plotting script that Codon is being tried out, with the CODON_PYTHON export showing the Python-interop path being exercised.

name: Practica-AP3
summary: An algorithms practical solving a problem three ways -- exhaustive search, greedy and a metaheuristic -- against a public benchmark set with a supplied checker. The runner compiles the chosen solver with codon build, so Codon is how the submissions are made fast enough to pass the time limits.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from runner.sh compiling the solver with codon build against a timed benchmark set that Codon supplies the speed the practical requires.

name: 0num4/codontest
summary: A trial of Codon with its own CI workflow. The README records where it stopped: an attempt to run an existing script failed because Codon would not resolve the modules it imported, so the author rebuilt the environment under poetry. A record of the module-resolution wall rather than a working port.
why_codon: README describes trying Codon for speed and hitting module resolution, linking a Japanese article on why Codon is fast.
note: One of the few entries recording a failure. Worth keeping: an index of successful uses would misrepresent what adopting Codon is like.

name: PisP-dsl
summary: A small domain-specific language project with a Codon directory holding the solver, an analysis script and a cmd.txt recording the install steps -- the exaloop install script and the PATH export needed to reach the compiler.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from a Codon directory carrying the solver alongside its install notes that Codon was tried as the execution path for the DSL's programs.

name: ctfcup24-school-ad
summary: Attack-and-defence infrastructure for a 2024 capture-the-flag competition. One service, flysim, is built on Codon: the deployment pins a specific version through an install script, and an exploit written against it ships a session_authenticator in Codon. Codon appears on both sides, as the service's implementation and inside the attack.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from a pinned Codon install script in the service deployment and a Codon session authenticator in the exploit that Codon is the service's runtime.
note: The only security-competition entry, and the only one where Codon appears in an exploit as well as in a service.

name: akleemans/aoc-2022
summary: Advent of Code 2022 solutions in Python with a codon-test directory holding a runner, so the same puzzle code can be executed compiled as well as interpreted.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from a dedicated codon-test directory with its own runner beside the Python solutions that Codon is being compared against interpreted Python.

name: akleemans/aoc-2023
summary: Advent of Code 2023 solutions by the same author, where the Codon experiment has been promoted from a side directory into a top-level run_codon.py driving the whole year's puzzles.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from run_codon.py sitting at the top level, a year after the same author kept Codon in a test directory, that the experiment was carried forward.
note: The pair is the only two-year longitudinal case in the index: the same author's Codon usage grew between 2022 and 2023.
